attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, written in his voice.

semantics.note: The restored wording matches the source. The sentence mixes a loose technical description with evaluative language ('passing that off', 'coddles'). It is a characterisation inside a rhetorical passage, and no model population or frequency is stated.

contract.note: The contract rightly finds no test that settles the whole statement. 'Summary' and 'intelligence' have no definition the speaker supplied, and 'coddles' could mean sycophancy, tone or reassurance. Treating it as untestable is fair.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed Nature study (Apr 2026): models trained to be warm validated incorrect beliefs more often. This bears on a narrow sycophancy reading for trained variants only, not on all LLMs or on whether the label intelligence fits.

Anthropic's own disclosure (Mar 2025) of a model combining facts in multi-step reasoning. This challenges a mere-regurgitation reading but is compatible with learning from past data. It is a company disclosure, not an independent finding.

reviews.rationale: The statement is an evaluative characterisation. Whether LLM output is 'passed off' as intelligence depends on an undefined standard, and 'summary' and 'coddles' each have several readings. The evidence touches narrow parts (sycophancy, internal reasoning) but cannot score the claim as written.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The Anthropic/OpenAI rental exclusion is kept as a scope limit. 'Few signs that will change' fairly renders the forward clause as a present observation about the signs available. The 'anecdotes and copium' dismissal is rhetorical colour.

contract.note: Reading 'economic value' as demonstrated commercial or productivity benefit in Q2 2026 is ordinary and fair. Whether recommender or ads GPUs count as 'AI GPUs', and the undefined 'very little' threshold, both drive the result.

evidence.note: Meta's Q2 2026 earnings call reports AI-driven gains in ad clicks and conversions and a large Advantage+ run-rate, outside the excluded rentals. These are company self-reports: they do not isolate GPU contribution or net benefit, and they cover one firm.
Meta Engineering post (Oct 2026) says its GEM ads model trains on thousands of GPUs. It links GPUs to commercial use but postdates the target period and Zitron's post, and it is a company disclosure.

reviews.rationale: Meta's self-reported ad gains suggest some value outside the excluded rentals. But they are company disclosures that do not isolate GPU-attributable net benefit, and no representative independent measure exists for Q2 2026. The packet does not settle whether the value was 'very little'.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Firm 'will' with the antecedent 'when this ends' kept. The proposition omits the 'why nobody stopped it' and rationalising clauses, 'even if they hate the companies', and the causal 'because' clause, but the core commitments are kept.

contract.note: Requiring a documented end of the boom described in the post, then broad public (not corporate) demand for a bailout, is a fair plain reading. The speaker gave no definition of the bubble ending and no threshold for 'many'.

evidence.note: TechRadar (Oct 27, 2026), citing Reuters, reports a steep fall in Chinese AI and chip stocks. This is regional market stress. It does not show the hyperscaler/NVIDIA boom ended or any public demand for a bailout.

reviews.rationale: Nothing in the packet shows the antecedent (the end of the AI boom Zitron described) happened, so the conditional forecast is not scored. A decline confined to Chinese stocks does not meet the early-resolution rule, and no deadline was stated.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post. The quoted phrases are ones he puts in others' mouths, not the assessed inference.

semantics.note: Faithfully captures his inference: no other willing or capable buyer at that size, and not enough diverse demand. The separate prediction about how the deal will be portrayed is rightly left out.

contract.note: Reading 'anyone else' as a credible alternative buyer on comparable terms, and 'diverse demand' as capacity-weighted commitments from multiple customers, is a fair ordinary reading. Without bid or concentration data, the reading decides what would count.

evidence.note: Lambda's own Aug 27, 2026 release says it has tens of thousands of customers across several categories. It gives no spending distribution and no sign of another buyer at about $35B, and it is a company disclosure.

Lambda's Nov 2025 announcement of a multibillion Microsoft deal, page updated Oct 2026. It shows another large customer, but it is earlier, its value is undisclosed and the capacity differs, so it is not a comparable competing bid.

reviews.rationale: No bids, sales pipeline or customer-concentration data in the packet show whether another buyer could have taken comparable capacity, or whether demand was diverse enough. Lambda's own disclosures of a broad customer base and a Microsoft deal neither confirm nor refute the inference.
